name: Crucible Industries Thermal Cascade TC-5 'Flashover'
description:
A directed energy weapon that fires a microwave pulse calibrated to ignite specific materials at range. The Flashover does not burn targets directly — instead, it rapidly heats flammable materials in the target area (clothing, paper, wood, fuel, solvents) past their ignition point, causing them to spontaneously combust. The result is an apparently natural fire that starts simultaneously at every point within the beam's focus.

Crucible designed the TC-5 for infrastructure denial — destroying enemy supplies, equipment, and facilities through fire without leaving evidence of an incendiary weapon. The microwave pulse is invisible and silent, and the resulting fire appears to start from material failure rather than external ignition. Arson investigators trained to look for pour patterns and ignition points find nothing, because the ignition source was a directed energy beam that left no physical trace.

The Flashover's anti-personnel effect is incidental but devastating. Clothing ignites while being worn. Hair combusts. Synthetic materials melt. A target struck by the TC-5 does not experience being shot — they experience spontaneous combustion.
specifications:
caliber: N/A — calibrated microwave ignition pulse
effective_range: 10-200 meters
rate_of_fire: 1 pulse per 5 seconds
capacity: 10 pulses per power cell
weight: 9.6 kg
power_source: Dedicated thermal-calibrated power cell
tactical_use: The Flashover is deployed for covert infrastructure destruction and deniable incendiary attacks. The weapon's ability to cause fires that appear spontaneous makes it invaluable for operations where plausible deniability is required. Operators target ammunition stores, fuel depots, vehicle fleets, and document archives — anything flammable that an enemy needs to function. The fire appears natural, the cause is untraceable, and the destruction is comprehensive.
cultural_context: The TC-5 has created a persistent paranoia about spontaneous fires in GLMZ. When a warehouse burns without apparent cause, or a vehicle fleet ignites simultaneously, people wonder if a Flashover was responsible. Crucible has never publicly acknowledged the weapon's existence, but the pattern of untraceable fires following corporate disputes is difficult to explain by coincidence. Insurance investigators have begun consulting directed energy experts when fire investigations find no conventional ignition source.
story_hooks: A residential block in the lower tiers experienced simultaneous combustion — every flammable material in a 50-meter radius ignited at the same moment. The fire department recorded 200 simultaneous ignition points. No natural cause explains the event, but no weapon was found.

A former Crucible engineer is selling TC-5 frequency calibration data on the black market. With this data, anyone with sufficient microwave generation equipment could build a crude Flashover equivalent — and someone is buying.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular directed-energy rifle with a distinctly thermal aesthetic. The TC-5 resembles a precision instrument crossed with a furnace — all sharp lines, heat-dissipation geometry, and purposeful engineering. The profile is aggressive but refined, suggesting expensive military heritage rather than street-level hardware.
physical_description.dimensions: 127 cm length, 8 cm width at widest point, 6.5 cm height at receiver. Barrel assembly extends 43 cm from muzzle brake to receiver.
physical_description.weight_description: Heavy but well-balanced — 9.6 kg distributed across the frame so it sits naturally in a two-handed grip. The weight suggests dense materials and serious engineering, not a light carbine. Feels purposeful and deliberate in hand.
physical_description.primary_material: Aircraft-grade aluminum alloy chassis with titanium heat-dissipation fins. Barrel assembly is composite ceramic-lined to withstand thermal cycling. Receiver housing is reinforced polymer-metal laminate.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with brushed titanium accents on the heat-sink fins. Scorch marks and thermal discoloration marks expected around the barrel and upper receiver. Polymer sections show micro-stress fractures from repeated thermal expansion.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with brushed titanium silver on cooling fins and barrel assembly. Accents of deep red on targeting reticle housing and power management ports. The overall effect is industrial and austere.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer grip with embedded thermal-feedback channels — textured for purchase even with gloved hands. The grip is textured crosshatch pattern with subtle temperature-sensitive coloration that shifts under operational heat.
distinctive_features: Prominent radial cooling fins running the length of the barrel assembly, suggesting extreme thermal management requirements
Recessed targeting laser port below the rail system with faint crimson lens
Segmented barrel shroud with visible thermal vents spaced evenly along the weapon's length
Large secondary power indicator on the left side of the receiver — a segmented bar that glows orange-amber during operation
Ceramic-lined muzzle brake with visible heat stress and oxidation patterns
Rail-mounted thermal management display integrated into the top receiver
Reinforced magazine well (for power cells) with locking lugs that appear scored from heavy use
Crucible Industries serial plate flush-mounted on the right side, marked with military registry stamps
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: CRUCIBLE INDUSTRIES logo embossed on the left side of the receiver in brushed chrome. Below it, military restriction stamps in red: INCENDIARY AUTHORIZATION REQUIRED. Serial number and manufacturing date stamped on right side of chassis in small, precise numerals. Specification plate on the magazine well details thermal parameters and power requirements.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units show heavy thermal stress — scorch marks around the muzzle, discoloration on the barrel fins from repeated thermal cycling, micro-fractures in the polymer grip from grip pressure under operational heat. Cosmetic wear from transport and handling, but mechanical integrity is maintained. The weapon is brutally practical, not showpiece-clean.
